overall: The AG found the Somerset School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by requiring permission to record, by under-specific notices naming no negotiating parties, and by discussing the superintendent search in executive session. No email deliberation was found. The Committee was ordered to amend minutes and release executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Chair required attendees at the March 20 and April 4 meetings to seek permission before recording; no April 4 meeting occurred.
allegations.key_passage: In its response to the complaints, the Committee acknowledged that the Chair made a mistake during its March 20 meeting by suggesting that attendees needed to seek permission from, rather than simply notify, the Chair prior to recording the meeting.

allegations.summary: Notices for the March 20 and April 3 meetings did not name the unions or non-union personnel whose contracts were to be negotiated in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee failed to identify in the notice for its March 20 and April 3 meetings the union or non-union personnel with whom it was negotiating.

allegations.summary: Notice for the April 4 meeting allegedly lacked executive session topic detail; the Committee did not meet that day.
allegations.key_passage: We find no violation with respect to an April 4 meeting notice because the Committee did not meet on April 4.

allegations.summary: Committee met in executive session on April 3 to discuss appointments to and progress of a Superintendent Search Committee, a topic outside the enumerated purposes.
allegations.key_passage: This topic was not appropriate under any of the ten enumerated executive session purposes.

allegations.summary: Alleged that Committee members improperly deliberated by email about the Superintendent Search Committee appointments.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find sufficient evidence that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law in this manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Within 30 days, amend the March 20 and April 3 open session minutes to identify the unions and non-union personnel whose contracts were discussed in executive session.
Within 30 days, release to the public the portions of the April 3 executive session minutes concerning appointments to and the progress of the Superintendent Search Committee.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
